claims.explanation: PU-H71 is an Hsp90 inhibitor that preferentially kills cancer cells dependent on Hsp90 client oncoproteins. Sensitivity is likely driven by high expression or activation of Hsp90 clients such as mutant EGFR, BRAF, MET, and JAK2, which are known to be destabilized by PU-H71. Conversely, protective features include intact apoptotic signaling (e.g., wild-type TP53) and expression of Hsp90 co-chaperones or anti-apoptotic proteins that buffer against Hsp90 inhibition.

features.basis: Mutant EGFR is an Hsp90 client; PU-H71 degrades it, and EGFR-mutant lines are among the most sensitive.
Mutant BRAF is an Hsp90 client; PU-H71 induces its degradation, and BRAF-mutant lines are enriched in sensitive group.
MET is an Hsp90 client; PU-H71 depletes MET and may sensitize MET-mutant tumors.
JAK2 is an Hsp90 client; PU-H71 degrades JAK2 and is effective in JAK2-mutant MPN models.
BCL-6 depends on Hsp90; PU-H71 destabilizes BCL-6 and kills BCL-6-dependent DLBCL cells.
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, but wild-type TP53 may enhance apoptosis; however, many sensitive lines have TP53 mutations, so this is weak.
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK signaling, which may increase dependence on Hsp90 clients; NF1 mutations appear in several sensitive lines.
PTEN loss activates PI3K-AKT signaling, which is Hsp90-dependent; PTEN mutations appear in sensitive lines.
PIK3CA mutations may increase Hsp90 client load; observed in several sensitive lines.
KRAS mutations are more common in resistant lines, possibly due to alternative survival pathways.
HSPA1A upregulation by PU-H71 in virtual cell suggests a compensatory heat shock response that may reduce sensitivity.
MYC is an Hsp90 client and its downregulation by PU-H71 may contribute to cell death; high MYC expression could predict sensitivity.
